title: Arbitrary-base-change and etale functoriality of a section Rees family
statement:
Let $S$ be a Noetherian scheme (one admitting a finite affine cover by spectra of Noetherian rings), let $d\geq0$, and let $g:V\to S$ be smooth, separated and of finite type of pure relative dimension $d$, with a closed section $s:S\hookrightarrow V$, $g s=1_S$.
For the ideal $\mathcal I$ of $s(S)$ set $\mathcal E=\mathcal I/\mathcal I^2$, $\pi:N_s=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_S\operatorname{Sym}(\mathcal E)\to S$, with zero section $z$. Set $D_sV=\underline{\operatorname{Spec}}_V\mathcal O_V[t,\mathcal I/t]$, using the subalgebra of $\mathcal O_V[t,t^{-1}]$ generated by $t$ and the $b/t$, $b\in\mathcal I$. Its structural map is $q:D_sV\to\mathbf A^1_S$ and its section $\sigma$ is the augmentation $t\mapsto t$, $\mathcal I/t\mapsto0$, with coefficients restricted by $s$.
For every morphism $v:S'\to S$ of Noetherian schemes, put $V'=V\times_SS'$, with induced section $s'$ and ideal $\mathcal I'$. The canonical map
$$D_{s'}V'\longrightarrow D_sV\times_SS'$$
is an isomorphism, commuting with $t$, the augmented sections, the punctured trivializations, and the identifications of the pairs at $0$ and $1$. The conormal map $v^*\mathcal E\to\mathcal E'$ and the induced normal-bundle map are isomorphisms. On a centred etale affine chart and an arbitrary affine base extension $R\to R'$, writing $B'=B\otimes_RR'$, $P'=R'[x]$, $I'=(x)B'$, the algebra identification is
$$B[t,I/t]\otimes_RR'\cong B'\otimes_{P'}R'[t,u]\cong B'[t,I'/t],$$
with $t\mapsto t$, $b\mapsto b\otimes1$, $x_j/t\mapsto x'_j/t$, and $[x_j]\mapsto[x'_j]$ on conormals. No flatness of $v$ is required. The new structural maps remain smooth separated of dimension $d$ and compactifiable.
If $h:V_1\to V$ is separated etale of finite type over $S$, $g_1=gh$ has a closed section $s_1$ with $h s_1=s$, and the square of centres is Cartesian, then
$$D_{s_1}V_1\cong D_sV\times_VV_1.$$
In particular its map to $D_sV$ is etale and preserves sections and both fibres. For an affine chart $B\to B_1$, with $I_1=IB_1$, its algebra map is $B_1\otimes_B B[t,I/t]\cong B_1[t,I_1/t]$. At zero its map is precisely the linear isomorphism of normal bundles induced by $[b]\mapsto[h^\sharp b]$ on conormals; at one it is $h$. All these canonical identifications agree on restrictions.
The scheme, morphism, algebra and coefficient notation and the specified comparison maps are those of [def-pc-scheme], [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf], [def-sbc-affine-space], [def-asd-vector-bundle-zero-section], [lem-pur-conormal-graded-algebra], [def-asd-compactifiable], [def-weil-etale-morphism], [def-pc-fibre-product].

proof.text: Construct Laurent comparison data by applying the Laurent-polynomial functor to each affine coefficient map. Construct zero-fibre data by quotienting each extended-Rees map by t. Naturality follows from the coefficient-map naturality and quotient extensionality. PullbackData.comparison_comp_relativeGluingMap gives compatibility with the maps into the Rees family and the polynomial line. Quotient-polynomial comparison data give augmented-section compatibility. The lift of the unit section into the Laurent chart is natural, by the polynomial pullback square and cancellation of the open immersion; composing proves one-fibre compatibility. Projection compatibility and all three chart formulas are PullbackData.comparison_toBase and its chart formula. Cancel the closed immersion of the zero fibre to obtain zero-section compatibility. This proves Compatible for any commuting pair of closed sections over the bases.

source.place: Local construction, explicit base-change maps and etale maps of pairs; old item Steps 5–6.

proof.text: For arbitrary base change the canonical conormal comparison is an epimorphism by Cartesian conormal base change. Centred coordinates make both conormals finite locally free of the same rank d, and pullback preserves this rank. At every stalk, exactness of the module stalk functor preserves the epimorphism, and both stalk modules are finite free of rank d. Identify the two free modules by a rank isomorphism: a surjective endomorphism of a finite module is injective, hence the original stalk map is bijective. Stalkwise detection gives IsIso of the specified conormalMap. This works also in rank zero.

proof.text: For an etale pair with Cartesian centres the new kernel ideal is the pullback of the old kernel. On every affine pair the new ideal is therefore the mapped ideal. Etaleness makes each affine coefficient map flat, so the proved source-library flat extended-Rees pushout gives the chart pushout. Apply PullbackData.isPullback_comparison; etaleness is preserved by this pullback. Cartesian flat conormal base change proves IsIso of conormalMap directly.

proof.text: The extended-Rees map sends t to t, so its t-ideal maps to the new t-ideal. The quotient-ring pushout square, pasted with each Rees chart pushout, gives a pullback square of normal cones over the ambient schemes. For a section, normalConeProj followed by the section equals the ambient normal-cone map, by purityNormalProjection_eq and the closed-immersion lift equation. Cancel the Cartesian square of centres. The normal comparison is thus a pullback of the identity on S and is an isomorphism. Its equality with the zero map already fixed in Compatible follows by cancelling the closed immersion into the Rees space.

proof.text: For normal_bundle, centred coordinates give finite local freeness of rank d and invertibility of symmetricComparison. Take the existing normalized reesConeComparison and the isomorphism induced by the symmetric-algebra anti-equivalence. Their composite is definitionally the coneToBundle map specified by section geometry; transfer its projection and zero-section formulas. All comparisons above are fixed chartwise by the coefficient maps, including their quotients by t, so restriction compatibility uses the same naturality equations.
